properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued September 16 at 2:46AM PDT until September 16 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Elko NV
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING FOR FWZ 426 & 427 WEDNESDAY...

...RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 11
AM TO 8 PM PDT THURSDAY FOR DRY, WINDY CONDITIONS FOR FIRE
WEATHER ZONES 426 AND 427...

The National Weather Service in Elko has issued a Red Flag
Warning, which is in effect from 11 AM to 8 PM PDT Thursday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire weather zones 426 and 427.

* WIND...Sustained southerly winds of 20-25 mph with gusts of
30-35 mph.

* HUMIDITY...Afternoon values of 10-15% possible

* IMPACTS...any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A red flag warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

NWSheadline: RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 11 AM THIS MORNING TO 8 PM PDT THIS EVENING FOR DRY, WINDY CONDITIONS FOR FIRE WEATHER ZONES 426 AND 427

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 16 at 4:46AM CDT until September 17 at 10:41AM CDT by NWS Omaha/Valley NE
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Iowa...

East Nishnabotna River At Red Oak affecting Montgomery County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...East Nishnabotna River at Red Oak.

* WHEN...Until Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Lowland flooding begins along the west
bank.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:00 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 20.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 4:00 AM CDT Wednesday was 20.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
this afternoon and continue falling to 7.7 feet early Monday
morning.
- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 20.3
feet on 05/29/1962.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at water.noaa.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 1045 AM CDT.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 16 at 4:17AM CDT until September 16 at 3:30PM CDT by NWS Des Moines IA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall
continues.

* WHERE...Adair County in southwestern Iowa...

* WHEN...Until 330 PM CDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 414 AM CDT, numerous roads remain closed in the warned area,
with water nearing Highway 25 south of Greenfield. Flooding is
already occurring. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain have fallen.
- An additional 1 inch or more is possible in the warned area
through this morning. Impacted streams include the Middle River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Greenfield, Stuart, Adair, Fontanelle, Orient, Bridgewater,
Greenfield Municipal Airport and Nodaway Park.
- This includes Interstate 80 between mile markers 73 and 96.
properties.instruction:
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

For the latest stream observations and forecasts refer to
weather.gov/desmoines/water.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 16 at 3:09AM EDT until September 16 at 7:00AM EDT by NWS Wilmington OH
properties.description:
FFWILN

The National Weather Service in Wilmington has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Mercer County in west central Ohio...

* Until 700 AM EDT.

* At 309 AM EDT, radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy rain
across the warned area. Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 1.5 inches are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Celina, Coldwater, St. Henry, Fort Recovery, Rockford, Wabash,
Mendon, Chickasaw, Montezuma, Tama, Carthagena, Neptune,
Chattanooga and Maria Stein.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

To report flash flooding, go to our website at weather.gov/iln and
submit your report via social media, when you can do so safely.
